title: Move store validation into a FormRequest
summary: Pull the inline validate out into StorePostRequest, then trip over the stub authorize.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class PostController extends Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request)
    {
        $validated = $request->validate([
            'title' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'],
            'body' => ['required', 'string'],
            'published_at' => ['nullable', 'date'],
        ]);

        $post = $request->user()->posts()->create($validated);

        return redirect()->route('posts.show', $post);
    }
}

turns.user: validate inline in PostController@store is ugly. move it to a FormRequest

assistant.body: Great call! The rules move into StorePostRequest and the controller only takes validated(). Separation of concerns, the Laravel way.
Apologies, I missed that. The make:request stub ships an authorize() that returns false, and I left it in. The auth middleware on the route already decides who is logged in, so this one returns true.

turns.user: also titles that long break the layout, cap at 100. oh and published_at should only be in the future

assistant.body: Two changes. max:255 becomes max:100, and published_at gains after:today. nullable stays, so an empty value still goes through as a draft.
